Drugs such as lidocaine or bupivacaine have been given by inhalation in severe intractable cough (p.1547), including cough caused by malignant neoplasms.1-4 Cough suppression is produced by an indirect peripheral action on sensory receptors, but as all protective pulmonary reflexes may be lost and bron- chospasm may be induced, nebulised local anaesthetics should be used in controlled circumstances only; there may also be tem- porary loss of the swallowing reflex.
